chapter_title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths

12.original: [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning]
12.content: which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning

fills.notes: Contrasting the three great days (works of liberation) with “deaths”: the first ‘death’ here is the primordial mixing of Darkness with the five sons—i.e., the initial death-state of Light by mixture, not moral death.
Fits the triadic schema: first/second/third ‘day’ each defined as a ‘time when…’.

fills.fill: and he shows them the glory of his greatness
fills.notes: After ‘unveils over them his image’, the next action in the oldest register is manifestation of Glory/Greatness to the enthroned victors; avoids later devotional phrasing.

fills.fill: from their aeons into his light
fills.notes: The line ‘and he raises them up … and he receives them into his hidden treasury’ demands a motion upward/out of their allotted aeons into the Father’s own Light (treasury = inmost preservation).
Syntactic necessity: ‘and he gives [to them from] his soul’ matches the subsequent ‘pour out upon them … his ambrosia’. It is distribution from the Father’s own substance (Life).
The clause ‘He can pour out upon them ... his ambrosia’ needs a simple connective (‘and’) in this register; the object list then follows (‘ambrosia and sweet perfume’).
Typical exclamatory particle before ‘fullness and a joy eternal!’; preserves the impersonal doxological style without inserting later liturgical expansions.
The sentence contrasts former hiddenness with a completed unveiling; anchoring it ‘in the great third day’ ties ¶11 back to ¶9’s third-day unveiling as the decisive moment.

fills.fill: which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning
fills.notes: Accepted as fitting the substrate: cosmological ‘reckoning/measure’ language (ordering of times by number) is characteristic of impersonal correspondential instruction.

The ‘living soul’ here is the world-soul/breath-principle established in the cosmos; ‘was set in the world’ matches the impersonal cosmogonic diction and the preceding ‘from which they receive living breath’.

After loss of light/air/soul, they are ‘separated and swept away’ from the Last Statue toward the opposite region; ‘outer darkness’ is the correspondential opposite of the Statue’s gathered Light (kept minimal, not evangelical).
‘bound on …’ requires the instrument/state of binding; ‘their bonds’ preserves the mythic-judicial register without importing later penal language.

Parallel to the first death’s purifying ‘great fire’ but in opposite sense: for the sinners the female/demonic principle becomes ‘a fire’ of torment; keeps to elemental correspondences (fire as consuming passion in the opposite sense).

Bridges to ‘those three places’: their deeds ‘will lead them into those three places’ (a triadic distribution of punitive regions). This is the minimal verb required by the syntax and cosmological causality.

assessment: Most gaps are syntactically and structurally constrained by the three-day/ two-death schema. The largest uncertainties are in ¶15 where the punitive geography (‘those three places’) and the role of ‘the female’ are only partially preserved; restorations there are correspondentially consistent (movement away from gathered Light; binding; fire in opposite sense) but remain tentative without parallel witnesses.
